record.narrative: The first wave registers canonical and mechanistically plausible dependencies in a lung cancer cell-line CRISPR dataset. More negative dependency scores indicate stronger dependency, so most hypotheses use negative directions to represent stronger dependency in the exposed/aberrant group. The selected comparisons cover pathway drivers (KRAS mutation for KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E for BRAF dependency, EGFR or ERBB2 amplification for receptor-tyrosine kinase dependencies), synthetic-lethal tumor-suppressor relationships (TP53 wild-type vs loss for MDM2; KEAP1 loss for NFE2L2; SMARCA4 loss for SMARCA2), and known or plausible DNA damage/repair dependencies in MSI-high cancers (WRN and DHX9). MYC amplification is included for POLR2A because transcriptional amplification may increase transcriptional machinery dependency. Interaction claims test whether KRAS and EGFR dependencies are stronger within adenocarcinoma than in the complement lineage subtype. For the negative mean dependency scores, a clinically meaningful 10% relative difference corresponds roughly to a 0.025 absolute score shift around the observed -0.25 means, though I will judge each result against the comparator mean and uncertainty. All claims begin unresolved.

Running the full first-wave set of 12 mechanistically motivated associations in lung cancer cell-line CRISPR dependency scores. All claims use negative directions where stronger dependency means more negative dependency score, except the MDM2 wild-type versus TP53-loss formulation, which also expects a stronger MDM2 dependency in TP53 wild-type lines and is signed accordingly. I am requesting all currently available registered comparisons now because the dataset is large, the predictors have adequate cell counts, and these comparisons will provide broad starting evidence across driver oncogenes, tumor-suppressor synthetic lethality, chromatin remodeling, DNA damage response, and transcriptional amplification hypotheses.

The first discovery wave separates robust associations from small, ambiguous, or contradicted effects. H9 and H10 are accepted: KEAP1-loss was not accepted because H8 was tested in the opposite direction. The raw KEAP1-loss contrast is strongly positive, approximately +0.80 score units, implying KEAP1-loss cells are much less dependent on NFE2L2 (higher/less negative dependency_NFE2L2). This is a large, precisely estimated effect far beyond the 10% clinical-significance scale, but it contradicts the registered hypothesis, so H8 is rejected and a reversed association is proposed. The small canonical-driver hypotheses H1, H3, H4, H5, H6, H7, H11, and H12 do not meet the accept standard: H1, H4, H6, H7, H11, and H12 have point estimates below or only marginally at the 10% relative-effect scale and include null in the 95% interval; H2 and H5 are imprecise interaction estimates with little support; H3's maximum claimed-direction support is below the clinical threshold and the point estimate is opposite, so H3 is closed. H4 is the most borderline potentially meaningful result, so I used the one voluntary validation request on H4 rather than on already robust effects. No leakage is apparent because predictors are measured genomic/molecular features and outcomes are dependency scores, but these are cross-sectional associations, not causal claims, and subgroup/interaction estimates remain uncertain.

The independent validation for H4 does not support accepting EGFR amplification as associated with stronger EGFR dependency. The discovery estimate was borderline relative to the 10% clinical threshold (signed effect +0.0252, 95% interval -0.0003 to +0.0507), but the validation estimate is near zero (+0.0015) with a wide adjusted interval (-0.0431 to +0.0461) that includes both no effect and effects larger than the threshold. I therefore leave H4 unresolved as an association that is not accepted, but close it because the available independent validation does not motivate additional analysis of the same main contrast. The KEAP1/NFE2L2 result is now best expressed as the reversed claim H13: KEAP1-loss cells have higher, less negative dependency_NFE2L2 scores, with a raw signed effect of about +0.80 (95% interval +0.78 to +0.82). This is a very large association far exceeding the clinical-significance scale, so I accept H13 and close the original rejected H8. The strong accepted findings remain SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency and MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency. The next wave focuses on whether robust associations are subtype-driven, whether chromatin-remodeler relationships extend to ARID1A co-loss, whether other DNA repair or p53 pathway dependencies emerge, and whether unassigned research markers explain additional dependency variation. These are dataset associations, not causal claims.

These proposals extend the currently accepted dataset associations rather than repeating them. The KEAP1/NFE2L2 reversed association is now registered in the correct direction in H13; the new interaction and library-restricted claims ask whether it is stronger in adenocarcinoma, whether it remains large in the dominant Avana screen library, and whether it is robust across measured screening context. Similarly, SMARCA4-loss-driven SMARCA2 dependency is tested for lineage heterogeneity and Avana-library robustness. MSI-high association with WRN is also checked within Avana, while additional DNA-repair hypotheses (BRCA2 loss with WRN/DHX9 and MSI-high with USP7) broaden the DNA damage response exploration. Reciprocal receptor-tyrosine-kinase hypotheses test amplification-specific cross dependencies: EGFR amplification associated with weaker ERBB2 dependency and ERBB2 amplification associated with weaker EGFR dependency. Finally, two unassigned marker claims probe whether research marker D or F predicts SMARCA2 or WRN dependency; their expected raw direction is deliberately uncertain, with the registered direction testing stronger dependency.

I requested 12 previously registered, untested comparisons selected to allocate investigation across focused follow-up and broad discovery. The focused set tests whether accepted dataset associations are lineage-specific or library-specific: adenocarcinoma KEAP1/NFE2L2 and adenocarcinoma MSI/WRN, and Avana-library-restricted SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 contrasts. The mechanistic set tests additional synthetic-lethal or pathway hypotheses: ARID1A loss for SMARCA2 dependency and SMARCA4 loss interaction with ARID1A loss; TP53 wild-type status for USP7 and RPL11 dependencies; BRCA2 loss for WRN dependency; and MSI-high for USP7 dependency. The marker set probes unassigned research assays, especially marker D with SMARCA2 and marker F with WRN/DHX9, because these may reveal additional associations even if they lack assigned biological roles. These are dataset-level associations; no causal inference or independent validation is implied.

This wave mostly confirms earlier strong associations and identifies one new strong association. H20 and H21 show that the KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 and MSI-high/WRN effects remain very large and precise within adenocarcinoma. H35 and H36 show the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 effects remain essentially unchanged when restricted to the dominant Avana screen library. These are accepted as dataset-level robustness confirmations; they do not establish causality or generalizability beyond this dataset. H14, H16, H42, and H43 do not support clinically meaningful stronger dependency: the point estimates are near zero or opposite, and the maximum claimed-direction interval support is below the approximate 10% relative-scale threshold for these outcomes, so they are rejected and closed. H22 is an ARID1A co-loss interaction on the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association; the point estimate is in the hypothesized direction but is small and imprecise, so it is unresolved and deferred rather than accepted. H37 is near null for BRCA2 loss and WRN dependency; although its wide interval includes some clinically meaningful negative values, the point estimate is essentially zero, so it is unresolved and closed. H39 is borderline: the signed estimate suggests MSI-high may have stronger USP7 dependency and the point estimate is plausibly meaningful, but the interval crosses null and could be confounded by p53 status, mutation burden, or screening context; it remains unresolved and active. H15 is the main new finding: TP53 wild-type versus TP53-loss cells show a raw USP7 dependency difference of about -0.396 (reported signed +0.396), with a narrow interval far above the clinical threshold and biologically plausible because wild-type p53 pathway states may increase USP7 dependency. I accept H15 and request independent validation because it is a new, large, pathway-level association and independent confirmation would be scientifically useful. Multiplicity and confounding remain concerns: these are unadjusted Welch comparisons in a cross-sectional cell-line dataset, and predictors may correlate with screen library, batch, growth pattern, ploidy, or mutation burden. I registered H15 stratification analyses in Avana, adenocarcinoma, and adherent culture, plus a USP7-MSI analysis restricted to TP53 wild-type cells, to test whether the new USP7 effect and the borderline MSI-USP7 signal are robust or confounded.

The independent validation for H15 strongly supports the TP53 wild-type/USP7 dependency association. Discovery evidence R15 gives a signed effect of +0.396 with 95% interval +0.325 to +0.467, and independent validation R26 gives +0.394 with a more conservative independent interval +0.290 to +0.498. The estimates are nearly identical, and the validation interval remains far above zero and above the approximate 10% clinically meaningful scale for this outcome. Therefore, within this supplied dataset, TP53 wild-type status is associated with stronger USP7 dependency relative to TP53-loss status. I accept H15 and close investigation of the main contrast because discovery plus independent validation have now settled that registered comparison. This is not a causal claim: TP53 loss is a measured cellular feature, but TP53 pathway state may be correlated with other genomic, copy-number, ploidy, mutation-burden, library, batch, or culture factors. The registered refinements H44-H47 test the TP53-WT/USP7 effect in the dominant Avana screen library, in adenocarcinoma, in adherent culture, and test whether the borderline MSI-high/USP7 signal is robust within TP53 wild-type cells; these are separate from the validated main contrast. The additional interaction proposals probe whether accepted synthetic-lethal-like associations are modified by co-occurring genomic states: KEAP1/NFE2L2 by KRAS mutation, SMARCA4/SMARCA2 by TP53 loss, MSI/WRN by KRAS mutation, and TP53/USP7 by KEAP1 loss. These remain dataset associations and may fail if subgroup cells are small or effects are context-dependent.

These new comparisons are focused refinements of the strongest accepted dataset associations. The goal is not to repeat the main effects, but to ask whether they persist after imposing biologically important contexts that could plausibly confound or modify them. For SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 dependency, I registered adenocarcinoma, ARID1A-wild-type, and low-mutation-burden restrictions to test whether the synthetic-lethal-like association is merely lineage-driven, ARID1A-co-loss-driven, or mutation-burden-driven. For KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 dependency, I registered adherent-culture and TP53-wild-type restrictions because the main reversed association is very large but may be sensitive to culture context or p53 co-alteration. For MSI-high/WRN dependency, I registered adherent-culture and TP53-wild-type restrictions to test whether the association is robust to culture and independent of p53 loss. For TP53 wild-type/USP7 dependency, I registered high-mutation-burden and KEAP1-wild-type restrictions because TP53 loss correlates with other pathway states and may be correlated with mutation burden or KEAP1 co-alteration. The expected directions follow the accepted claims: stronger dependency for SMARCA2, WRN, and USP7, and weaker/higher NFE2L2 dependency with KEAP1 loss. If these context-restricted estimates remain large and precise, they will support robust dataset-level associations; if they attenuate, that will motivate interaction or confounding-focused follow-up. These are still associations in a cross-sectional cell-line dataset, not causal claims.

I selected 12 untested existing claims to test robustness and possible confounding of the strongest accepted dataset associations while completing the most useful pending follow-ups. H52-H60 are the newly registered context restrictions: SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2 within adenocarcinoma, ARID1A wild-type, and low mutation burden; KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2 within adherent culture and TP53 wild-type; MSI-high/WRN within adherent culture and TP53 wild-type; and TP53 wild-type/USP7 within high mutation burden and KEAP1 wild-type. These ask whether the large effects are merely driven by lineage, co-alterations, mutation burden, culture context, or p53/KEAP1 co-state. I also included H34 and H44 to test whether the MSI-high/WRN and TP53 wild-type/USP7 associations remain in the dominant Avana screen library, because screening-library artifacts or library-specific screen quality could otherwise explain accepted effects. Finally, H47 tests whether the borderline MSI-high/USP7 signal remains within TP53 wild-type cells, separating a possible independent DNA-repair/MSS pathway association from confounding by TP53 state. This batch is deliberately focused on accepted or borderline accepted effects and likely confounders, rather than low-priority marker or reciprocal RTK broad exploration.

This wave largely establishes robustness of the main accepted dataset associations across several biologically relevant contexts. H52-H54 restrict SMARCA4-loss versus non-loss for SMARCA2 dependency to adenocarcinoma, ARID1A-wild-type cells, and low-mutation-burden cells. In all three restrictions, the signed effect remains about +0.77 to +0.78 with narrow intervals far from zero. This argues against the simple explanations that the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association is driven only by lineage, ARID1A co-loss, or low mutation burden. I therefore accept H52-H54 as dataset-level robustness confirmations and close those investigations.

H55-H56 restrict KEAP1-loss versus non-loss for NFE2L2 dependency to adherent culture and TP53-wild-type cells. The signed effects remain about +0.79 with tight intervals, showing that the large KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 association persists after these potential context or co-alteration restrictions. These are accepted and closed. H57-H58 restrict MSI-high versus non-MSI-high for WRN dependency to adherent culture and TP53-wild-type cells; the signed effects remain about +0.78 to +0.81 and precise. H34 additionally shows the MSI/WRN effect remains essentially unchanged within the dominant Avana screen library. Thus the MSI/WRN association is not merely a culture artifact, TP53-loss artifact, or Avana-library-specific screening artifact. These are accepted and closed.

For USP7, H44 shows the validated TP53-wild-type/TP53-loss association remains robust within the Avana library, with a signed effect about +0.40. This supports H44 and closes it. H59 restricts the TP53-wild-type/USP7 contrast to high mutation burden and yields a larger signed effect, about +0.48, with a precise interval well above clinical relevance. H60 restricts the contrast to KEAP1-wild-type cells and yields a signed effect about +0.37, also well above clinical relevance. These results suggest that the TP53-wild-type/USP7 association is robust to screening library and KEAP1 state and may be even stronger in higher mutation-burden contexts. I accept H60 and close it. I accept H59 but keep it active and request independent validation because it is a context-specific refinement with a large new point estimate; independent confirmation would be useful before closing it as a separate context association. This is not a causal claim: high mutation burden may correlate with MSI, DNA-repair defects, p53 pathway state, aneuploidy, or screening/context factors, and the observed modification could be confounded or biologically context dependent.

H47 tests whether the borderline MSI-high/USP7 signal survives within TP53-wild-type cells. The signed estimate is only +0.032 and the interval crosses zero, [-0.003, +0.068]. The point estimate is much smaller than the main accepted associations, and the uncertainty is insufficient to support a clinically meaningful MSI-high/USP7 association. Combined with the earlier borderline H39 result, I leave H47 unresolved but close it, and I close H39 as well to reduce low-priority follow-up. The evidence does not support accepting MSI-high as a robust predictor of USP7 dependency in this dataset.

Overall, the strongest conclusions remain dataset-level associations: SMARCA4 loss associates with stronger SMARCA2 dependency; KEAP1 loss associates with weaker/higher NFE2L2 dependency; MSI-high associates with stronger WRN dependency; and TP53-wild-type status associates with stronger USP7 dependency. The new results make these effects much less attributable to lineage subtype, ARID1A co-loss, low mutation burden, culture type, TP53-loss co-state, Avana library, or KEAP1 co-state. Residual confounding remains possible due to unmeasured pathway interactions, batch, screen quality, growth rate, media, ploidy, or co-alteration structure, and no result should be interpreted as causality or external generalizability.

The newly released validation evidence substantially sharpens the conclusion for USP7 and confirms that the main EGFR-amplification claim is not supported. H4 tested whether EGFR amplification is associated with stronger EGFR dependency. The discovery result was already weak: the signed estimate was only +0.025 and its lower bound touched zero. Independent validation is essentially null, with a signed estimate of +0.0015 and an independent interval spanning both sides of zero. There is no reproducible evidence of a clinically meaningful EGFR-dependency effect in this dataset, so I reject H4 and close it. This is a negative conclusion for the registered EGFR-amplification contrast, not proof that EGFR copy-number states never affect dependency; amplification may be a poor proxy for functional EGFR pathway activity or may be confounded by co-amplified loci.  H36 tests KEAP1 loss versus non-loss for NFE2L2 dependency restricted to the dominant Avana screen library. Discovery and independent validation are nearly identical, with signed effects of about +0.796 and +0.795 and tight intervals far above clinical relevance. I accept and close H36. This strongly argues that the large KEAP1/NFE2L2 association is not merely an Avana-library artifact within this dataset.  H59 tests TP53 wild-type versus TP53 loss for USP7 dependency restricted to higher mutation burden. Discovery gave a signed effect of +0.477, and independent validation gave +0.392 with an interval +0.239 to +0.545. Although the point estimate attenuates in validation, it remains far above clinically meaningful thresholds and in the same direction as the main TP53 wild-type/USP7 association. I therefore accept and close H59 as a robust dataset-level context confirmation. The attenuation is a useful caveat: TP53-loss cells and high mutation burden are biologically heterogeneous, and mutation burden may correlate with MSI, DNA-repair defects, p53 pathway state, aneuploidy, or screening artifacts. Thus the claim is that higher-mutation-burden cells in this dataset still show the TP53 wild-type/USP7 association, not that mutation burden causally amplifies USP7 dependency.  Overall, the accepted main dataset associations remain: SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency; KEAP1 loss with weaker/higher NFE2L2 dependency; MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency; and TP53 wild-type with stronger USP7 dependency. The USP7 association is now validated both overall and in the higher-mutation-burden context, and the KEAP1/NFE2L2 association is validated in the dominant screen library. The next priority is to validate or robustness-test the remaining accepted main effects, especially SMARCA4/SMARCA2 and MSI/WRN, while continuing to explore modification by co-alterations and context.

No assessments are due. I am registering three blocks of comparisons for follow-up. First, I will test whether the four strongest accepted dataset associations are robust in technically trustworthy or contextually relevant subsets: high screen quality, non-Avana CRISPR library, and high-serum culture. These are not new biological mechanisms per se, but they address whether accepted SMARCA4/SMARCA2, KEAP1/NFE2L2, MSI/WRN, and TP53/USP7 effects are artifacts of dominant screen batch, screen quality, library platform, or culture conditions. Second, I registered interaction tests asking whether co-occurring alteration burden or specific co-alterations modify the accepted effects, especially mutation burden, TP53 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MYC amplification. These are distinct from the existing pending lineage, KRAS, KEAP1, ARID1A, and TP53-loss restrictions already on the ledger. Third, I added a small broad-exploration set for untested genomic features and constructed marker assays, prioritizing outcomes with large variance or pathway plausibility. The robustness and interaction claims should have priority in the next analyze batch; the marker claims are exploratory because the markers are constructed assays with no assigned biological role. All comparisons remain dataset-level associations, not causal or generalizable claims.

I selected a technical and contextual robustness batch focused on the four strongest accepted dataset associations: SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2 dependency, MSI-high/WRN dependency, and TP53 wild-type/USP7 dependency. These are currently accepted or largely supported, but before relying on them for validation or broader conclusions, I want to see whether they persist in higher-quality screens, in the largest screen batch, and in high-serum culture conditions. H68-H71 restrict all four comparisons to screens above the median screen_roc_auc, addressing whether accepted effects are artifacts of poor-quality screens. H76-H79 restrict them to media_serum_pct >= 10, testing culture-context stability. H62-H65 restrict them to batch_a, testing a major batch-level confounding candidate. I did not select the non-Avana library tests in this batch because the smallest exposure groups, especially MSI-high, could be very small or fail the cell-size rule in the non-Avana subset. I also deferred co-alteration interaction tests and broader marker/genomic discovery claims for the next round. These analyses ask only whether the existing dataset-level associations are stable across important technical and culture contexts; they are not causal or external-generalizability claims.

All twelve newly delivered discovery results support the four central accepted dataset associations with very large, precise effects in the specified technical or culture contexts. H68-R41 restricts SMARCA4-loss versus non-loss to high-quality screens (screen_roc_auc >= 0.9555) and gives a signed effect of +0.791, interval [0.764, 0.819], with adequate cells. H76-R45 restricts the same SMARCA4/SMARCA2 contrast to high-serum culture and gives +0.799, interval [0.774, 0.824]. H63-R50 restricts it to the largest batch, batch_a, and gives +0.747, interval [0.709, 0.785]. Thus H68, H76, and H63 are accepted and closed as dataset-level robustness confirmations. This argues that the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2-dependency association is not driven only by low-quality screens, high-serum media, or absence/presence of batch_a effects. It does not constitute independent validation, because these are subsets of the same discovery dataset.

The KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2-dependency association similarly remains robust. H69-R42 gives +0.793, interval [0.764, 0.822] in high-quality screens; H77-R46 gives +0.814, interval [0.788, 0.840] in high-serum culture; and H64-R51 gives +0.812, interval [0.765, 0.858] within batch_a. All are accepted and closed. Given the earlier Avana-library confirmation and independent validation for the Avana restriction, the overall H13 KEAP1/NFE2L2 association is now well supported within this dataset, though still not proven causal or externally generalizable.

The MSI-high/WRN-dependency association also survives these technical and context restrictions. H70-R43 gives +0.790, interval [0.751, 0.829] in high-quality screens; H78-R47 gives +0.784, interval [0.746, 0.823] in high-serum culture; and H65-R52 gives +0.824, interval [0.766, 0.882] within batch_a. The exposed MSI-high cell in batch_a is small (37) but meets the pre-specified minimum cell-size rule, and the interval remains far above the clinical relevance threshold. These are accepted and closed. The H10 overall MSI/WRN association therefore appears robust to screen quality, serum context, and major batch restriction, but it still lacks direct independent validation.

The TP53-wild-type versus TP53-loss contrast for USP7 dependency remains strong and robust. H71-R44 gives +0.426, interval [0.332, 0.519] in high-quality screens; H79-R48 gives +0.443, interval [0.353, 0.532] in high-serum culture; and H62-R49 gives +0.417, interval [0.284, 0.550] within batch_a. All are accepted and closed. Combined with the already validated overall USP7 association and the high-mutation-burden validation, this makes the USP7 result the best-supported main association in the current evidence set.

The main scientific concern is not statistical direction but residual confounding and generalization. These are discovery-sample restrictions, not independent validation. The consistency across high-quality screens, serum context, and batch_a reduces but does not eliminate explanations involving unmeasured co-alterations, ploidy, growth rate, batch interactions, library effects, or synthetic assay artifacts. I request independent validation for H9 (SMARCA4 loss versus non-loss for SMARCA2 dependency) because H9 is a central accepted main association that has not yet received independent validation, has good discovery cell sizes, and has survived multiple within-dataset robustness restrictions. This validation should help distinguish a reproducible dataset-level association from discovery-sample noise or correlated context artifacts. No causal mechanism or external generalizability is being claimed.

The response-deadline validation for H15 confirms the central TP53-status/USP7 association. Discovery gave a signed effect of about +0.396, and independent validation gave about +0.394 with an independent interval +0.290 to +0.498. The effect is in the same direction, nearly identical in size, and its conservative independent interval is far from zero and well above the clinically meaningful threshold. Thus I accept H15 and keep it closed. This supports the dataset-level claim that TP53 wild-type status is associated with stronger USP7 dependency, but it does not establish that TP53 status causally regulates USP7 dependency or that the association generalizes beyond this screen.

The newly delivered validation for H9 strongly confirms the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2-dependency association. Discovery was a signed effect of about +0.784, and independent validation is +0.804 with independent interval +0.775 to +0.833. The validation point estimate is slightly larger, but the effect is extremely large relative to the dispersion of SMARCA2 dependency scores and the independent lower bound is far above zero and the clinical-relevance threshold. Combined with prior robustness across adenocarcinoma, ARID1A wild-type, low mutation burden, Avana screens, high-quality screens, high serum, and batch_a, this now makes SMARCA4 loss versus non-loss the best-supported synthetic-lethality-like association after USP7. I accept H9 and close it.

H13 and H10 remain accepted main associations but still have a different validation profile. H13 has independent validation for the KEAP1-loss contrast within the dominant Avana library and many robustness confirmations, but not yet direct independent validation of the unrestricted overall claim. H10 MSI-high/WRN has strong within-dataset robustness but no direct independent validation yet. These should be prioritized for validation in future appraise stages. For immediate analysis, I registered lower-mutation-burden mean tests for MSI/WRN and KEAP1/NFE2L2 to test whether those effects are merely proxies for higher mutation burden, and cross-coalteration interaction tests among the accepted predictors. The interactions ask whether co-occurring KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, or MSI-high status modifies the main associations. They are still only dataset-level association-modification claims. Biological interpretation remains provisional: the effects could reflect true synthetic-lethal biology, pathway-level dependencies, correlated genomic states, or unmeasured screening artifacts.

No assessments are due. I am registering three complementary blocks of follow-up for the four strongest accepted dataset associations. First, I registered mean-difference claims that test each accepted association while excluding a major co-alteration: SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2 dependency among TP53 wild-type cells, KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2 dependency among SMARCA4 wild-type cells, MSI-high/WRN dependency among SMARCA4 wild-type cells, and TP53 wild-type/USP7 dependency among SMARCA4 wild-type cells. These ask whether the effects are independent of correlated p53, chromatin, and MSI/SMARCA4 co-state, rather than being driven solely by co-occurrence of accepted predictors. Second, I registered low-quality-screen restrictions for the same four associations. The existing robustness tests used high screen_roc_auc; these new claims test whether the effects also persist in the lower-quality half of screens, which can reveal whether accepted effects are artifacts of only the best-performing screens. Third, I registered interaction tests among accepted predictors: SMARCA4 loss modified by MSI-high for SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss modified by MSI-high for NFE2L2 dependency, MSI-high modified by SMARCA4 loss for WRN dependency, and TP53 wild-type/USP7 modified by MYC amplification. These test effect modification by biologically relevant co-alteration combinations not already registered. All remain within-dataset association or modification claims and are not causal or generalizability claims.

I select the twelve claims just registered as follow-up to the four central accepted dataset associations. This batch is more informative than additional broad marker tests because it targets whether the accepted associations survive exclusion of major co-altering states and low-quality screen conditions, and whether they exhibit interactions among the accepted predictors themselves. H104 and H110 test SMARCA2/SMARCA4 and USP7/TP53 effects restricted to TP53 wild-type or SMARCA4 wild-type cells respectively, reducing the chance that each association is driven by correlated p53 or chromatin alterations. H105, H107, H109, and H111 test whether all four main associations persist in lower-quality screens, complementing the previously accepted high-quality-screen restrictions. H106 and H108 test KEAP1/NFE2L2 and MSI/WRN effects restricted to SMARCA4 wild-type cells, while H107 and H109 test their lower-quality-screen persistence. H112-H115 test interactions: SMARCA4 loss modified by MSI-high for SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss modified by MSI-high for NFE2L2 dependency, MSI-high modified by SMARCA4 loss for WRN dependency, and TP53 status modified by MYC amplification for USP7 dependency. These remain dataset-level association and effect-modification analyses; they do not establish causality or external generalizability.

The twelve new results mainly strengthen the four central accepted associations as within-dataset, robustness-restricted comparisons rather than independent confirmations. For SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2 dependency, H104 shows the association remains very strong among TP53 wild-type cells (R54: +0.787, 95% CI 0.766 to 0.809), and H105 shows it persists in the lower-quality screen half (R55: +0.778, 0.751 to 0.805). These are not independent validations, but they argue against a simple explanation that the SMARCA2 effect is confined to TP53-loss cells or only to higher-quality screens. For KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2 dependency, H106 (R56: +0.798, 0.775 to 0.821 among SMARCA4 wild-type cells) and H107 (R57: +0.798, 0.770 to 0.827 in lower-quality screens) support robustness to SMARCA4 co-alteration status and screen-quality restriction. For MSI-high/WRN dependency, H108 (R58: +0.795, 0.762 to 0.828 among SMARCA4 wild-type cells) and H109 (R59: +0.790, 0.744 to 0.836 in lower-quality screens) are similarly strong; the exposed MSI-high cell in H109 is small but meets the cell-size rule. For TP53 wild-type/USP7 dependency, H110 (R60: +0.417, 0.338 to 0.496 among SMARCA4 wild-type cells) and H111 (R61: +0.360, 0.251 to 0.469 in lower-quality screens) remain far from zero. I accept and close H104-H111 as robustness-restricted dataset-level confirmations, not as causal or externally generalizable findings.

The four interaction tests are less supportive. H112, H113, and H114 test whether MSI-high or SMARCA4-loss states modify the main SMARCA2, NFE2L2, and WRN effects. The interaction estimates are small (R62: -0.017; R63: -0.026; R64: -0.022), their intervals include zero, and the upper bounds for clinically meaningful modification are modest. I reject these as unsupported effect-modification claims and close them. H115, USP7 modified by MYC amplification, has a larger point estimate (R65: +0.134) but a wide interval including zero (CI -0.048 to 0.315), likely due to the smaller MYC-amplified contrast cells; I leave it unresolved rather than rejecting. The main residual concern remains correlated co-alterations, unmeasured genomic context, screen artifacts, and discovery-sample overfitting; these new subsets reduce but do not eliminate that concern. Because H10 is the remaining central accepted association without direct independent validation and has now survived several robustness restrictions, I request independent validation for H10.

The newly delivered validation substantially strengthens the central evidence set. H10 (MSI-high versus MSI-stable for dependency_WRN) now has independent validation: discovery R10 was a signed +0.790 (95% CI +0.760 to +0.819), and validation R66 is +0.812 with an independent interval +0.765 to +0.858. Because the claim direction is -1, these signed positive values mean MSI-high cells have more negative WRN scores, i.e., stronger WRN dependency. The validation interval excludes zero and the effect is far larger than the small effects seen in rejected null claims, so I accept H10 and close it as a robust within-dataset association. H36 (KEAP1 loss versus KEAP1 wild-type for dependency_NFE2L2 within Avana-library screens) is also independently validated: discovery R21 +0.796 (CI +0.774 to +0.818) and validation R40 +0.795 (independent CI +0.764 to +0.826). With direction +1, positive values indicate KEAP1-loss cells have higher NFE2L2 dependency scores, i.e., weaker NFE2L2 dependency. I accept and close H36 as a well-supported Avana-subset association. H59 (TP53 wild-type versus TP53-loss for dependency_USP7 among high mutation-burden cells) is independently validated as well: discovery R34 +0.477 (CI +0.379 to +0.576) and validation R39 +0.392 (independent CI +0.239 to +0.545). The validation estimate is somewhat smaller than discovery but still large, positive, and far above zero. I accept and close H59. These results, together with the already validated H9 (SMARCA4 loss -> stronger SMARCA2 dependency) and H15 (TP53 wild-type -> stronger USP7 dependency), give four internally reproducible dataset-level associations: SMARCA4 loss -> stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high -> stronger WRN dependency; KEAP1 loss -> weaker NFE2L2 dependency; and TP53 wild-type -> stronger USP7 dependency. For H13, the unrestricted KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 association remains accepted and active because the exact unrestricted claim has not yet received direct independent validation, although it is strongly supported by R8 discovery and by H36's independent Avana-subset validation. The most informative next step is therefore to obtain direct independent validation for H13 if eligible, while analyzing the already registered non-Avana robustness claims and mutation-burden interactions. Negative or unsupported findings include the expected KEAP1-loss stronger-NFE2L2 hypothesis in H8, EGFR amplification/EGFR dependency in H4, BRAF V600E/BRAF dependency in H3, ARID1A loss/SMARCA2 dependency in H14, TP53 status/RPL11 dependency in H16, research-marker associations in H42 and H43, and the rejected interaction claims H112-H114 showing little modification of the main SMARCA2, NFE2L2, and WRN effects by MSI-high or SMARCA4 loss. Unresolved uncertainty remains for non-Avana library replication, mutation-burden interactions, USP7 modified by MYC amplification (H115, positive but wide interval), and external generalizability or causal mechanism. I registered new co-alteration-exclusion refinements to ask whether the main associations persist when the other major accepted predictor state is excluded (KEAP1 wild-type for SMARCA2 and WRN; MSI wild-type for USP7 and NFE2L2), while keeping all claims as dataset-level associations rather than causal claims.

No assessments are currently due. The central accepted evidence is now unusually reproducible within this dataset: SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, MSI-high is associated with stronger WRN dependency, and TP53 wild-type status is associated with stronger USP7 dependency. The next most informative step is not to chase weak novel markers, but to test whether these large effects are artifacts of guide library, correlated co-alteration state, or a small subset of screens.

I first register library-specific replication claims for the Ky library and, where cell sizes are safer, for the Humagne-CD library. If these effects persist across libraries with different guide sets, that makes screen-specific library artifacts less likely. If they differ, it shows that the current evidence may be library-dependent, which is important because the main Avana subset already has independent validation. I include Ky claims for all four central associations and Humagne-CD claims for SMARCA4/SMARCA2 and TP53/USP7; I avoid a Humagne-CD WRN claim because the MSI-high cell would likely be too small.

I also register cross-coalteration exclusion refinements that ask whether the accepted effects survive when another major accepted predictor state is absent: SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2 dependency among MSI-stable cells, KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2 dependency among ARID1A wild-type cells, TP53 wild-type/USP7 dependency among MYC non-amplified cells, and MSI-high/WRN dependency among ARID1A wild-type cells. These complement H116-H119 and help distinguish a direct-like association from one driven by correlated genomic state. All remain within-dataset associations and do not establish causality or external generalizability.

I am requesting 12 registered claims that directly interrogate the four central accepted associations from different angles of robustness, rather than adding weak new marker tests. The first block tests the effects outside the dominant Avana screen library: H72, H73, and H75 ask whether SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2, KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2, and TP53 wild-type/USP7 associations replicate in non-Avana screens. H120, H121, and H123 then test the larger Ky library specifically for the same three outcomes. This distinguishes a broad biological association from one created by a single guide-library or screen-quality artifact. I deliberately omit the WRN/MSI-high non-Avana and Ky claims (H74 and H122) because H34's Avana cell count implies too few MSI-high cells outside Avana to satisfy the 20-observation rule reliably. The second block requests co-alteration exclusions: H116-H119 test whether the main effects persist when KEAP1-loss or MSI-high status is excluded, and H126/H128 add two important exclusions for SMARCA4 loss among MSI-stable cells and TP53 wild-type/USP7 among MYC-amplification-negative cells. Together, these tests examine whether the accepted associations depend on correlated genomic state or guide-library composition. They remain within-dataset association tests, not causal or generalizability claims.

The new results substantially strengthen the central within-dataset associations, although they remain robustness subsets rather than external validation. For SMARCA4-loss versus SMARCA2 dependency, the non-Avana screens give a very large same-direction effect (R67: +0.801, CI 0.748 to 0.853), and Ky-library screens give +0.816 (CI 0.777 to 0.856); both support the already validated H9. For KEAP1 loss versus NFE2L2 dependency, non-Avana and Ky screens also reproduce the large weakened-dependency association (R68: +0.794, CI 0.746 to 0.842; R71: +0.794, CI 0.752 to 0.837), supporting H13 beyond the Avana-only subset. For MSI-high versus WRN dependency, exclusions of KEAP1-loss and MSI-stable/ARID1A states remain very strong where tested (R74: +0.787; R76: +0.798), consistent with the validated H10 effect being robust to some major co-alterations. For TP53 wild-type versus USP7 dependency, the co-alteration exclusion claims remain large and precise (R75 among MSI-stable +0.401; R78 among MYC-amplification-negative +0.376), supporting H15. However, the library-restricted USP7 results are more nuanced: non-Avana aggregate gives +0.321 but with a small comparator cell and a lower bound only +0.085 (R69), and Ky-library gives +0.212 (CI 0.051 to 0.373, R72). These are directionally positive and statistically non-null, but smaller than Avana effects, so I accept the non-Avana aggregate claim but keep it active for magnitude uncertainty, and leave H123 unresolved because the Ky estimate suggests possible guide-library attenuation. The co-alteration exclusions H116-H119, H126, and H128 all have tight intervals far from zero and are accepted/closed. Overall, the evidence continues to support SMARCA4 loss -> stronger SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss -> weaker NFE2L2 dependency, MSI-high -> stronger WRN dependency, and TP53 wild-type -> stronger USP7 dependency as dataset-level associations, with an unresolved caveat that USP7/TP53 effect size may be smaller in some library subsets. I request independent validation for H13 because the unrestricted KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 association is central and, while strongly replicated across many subsets, has direct validation only for the Avana-restricted H36.

The delivered validations substantially strengthen the central evidence set and allow several key conclusions to be closed as dataset-level associations. H9 receives its direct independent validation response: discovery R9 and validation R53 are both large positive signed estimates under the negative direction, with validation R53 +0.804 and an independent interval +0.775 to +0.833. Because a signed positive value here corresponds to a more negative SMARCA2 dependency score in SMARCA4-loss cells, I accept H9 and close it: SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency in this dataset. The effect is far larger than the practical threshold used for these comparisons and is much larger than the null-like estimates seen in rejected comparisons. H13 now has direct independent validation of the unrestricted KEAP1-loss association: discovery R8 +0.796 and validation R79 +0.791, with the independent interval +0.763 to +0.820 excluding zero. Under direction +1, a positive signed estimate means KEAP1-loss cells have higher, less negative NFE2L2 dependency scores. I therefore accept and close H13 as evidence that KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The same validation also reinforces rejection of H8, the earlier stronger-dependency hypothesis, so the supported association is in the opposite direction of H8. H14, ARID1A loss versus SMARCA2 dependency, now has direct validation that is essentially null: R80 is -0.002 with interval -0.062 to +0.058. This is small relative to the supported central effects and not clinically meaningful, so I reject and close H14. Together, the direct validations support a core reproducible pattern in this dataset: SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high is associated with stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, and TP53 wild-type status is associated with stronger USP7 dependency. These are associations measured across many subset, library, screen-quality, and co-alteration restrictions, but they are not claims about causality or external generalizability. Negative or unsupported findings remain important: BRAF V600E does not support a BRAF-dependency association, EGFR amplification does not support a meaningful EGFR-dependency association, ARID1A loss does not support an SMARCA2-dependency association, and the tested research-marker comparisons are null or nonmeaningful. Interaction tests for major effect modification by MSI-high, SMARCA4 loss, or ARID1A status are also unsupported for the central SMARCA2, NFE2L2, and WRN associations. The main unresolved uncertainty is not whether the central associations exist in this dataset, but whether their magnitude is constant across genomic and screen context. The TP53/USP7 effect is robust in Avana, high mutation burden, and several co-alteration exclusions, but appears smaller in some Ky-library analyses, leaving H123 unresolved and H75 accepted with magnitude caution. The new proposal asks whether the TP53 wild-type USP7 effect is specifically attenuated in the Ky library relative to the complement, which is the most direct follow-up to that caveat. The next most informative analyses are therefore the registered mutation-burden interactions and remaining library or co-alteration subsets for the four central associations, not additional weak marker screening.
